title: HOMEPROV E9 seven-day run: pre-registration amendment 3 (relaunch under the smoke-tested interpreter)

amends.note: none of the three files is modified; amendment 1's code edit stands; amendment 2's START, end and run tag are replaced

defect.what: testbed/e9/run_e9.sh resolves its host interpreter as PY=$(command -v python3) (line 116). The amendment-2 launcher inherited a PATH on which python3 is /usr/bin/python3 (Python 3.9.6, the macOS system build), whereas every smoke run used <home>/miniconda3/bin/python3 (Python 3.13.11): e9s_smoke1, e9s_smoke2, e9s_smoke3, e9s_move and e9s_final each log 'python=Python 3.13.11'. The recorder snapshots are WAL-mode copies (SQLite header bytes 18-19 = 2, 2); the system interpreter could not open them read-only ('sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file', reproduced on a copy of the start snapshot, which the 3.13.11 interpreter opens).
effects: the start snapshot's event (events.jsonl line 13) has an empty 'db' field and is not valid JSON; exp/stages/e9_score.py skips lines that do not parse, so every snapshot (day ends, nights, backup, final) would have been missing at scoring
the day-4 backup step (run_e9.sh, after snapshot_db restore_backup) parses that event and opens the backup copy with the same interpreter, so the backup and the restore session would have failed
the snapshot files themselves were correct (taken in a container with the monitor image; quick_check ok; sha256 recorded)
defect.found: 2026-10-12, about 09:20 UTC, by the lead, reading the run log after the 07:00 start event

first_launch.stopped_utc: 2026-10-12T13:25:27Z (SIGTERM to run_e9.sh; its EXIT trap tore down)

pi_decision.question: E9 launched with the system Python 3.9, not the Python 3.13 every smoke run used; that Python cannot read the recorder snapshots ... How should I proceed?

first_launch.teardown: E9 containers removed; signing-key and operator volumes destroyed; the hub's configuration.yaml restored (sha256 0ac1834b72c92c93..., the original); hub restarted; stock monitor and anchor restored. The anchors' chains are not collected on an interrupted run.

kept_not_results.statement: nothing from the first launch is scored or reported as an E9 result; this amendment is its only account

relaunch.tag: e9_main2 (run_e9.sh refuses an existing run directory and existing outputs; e9_main's are kept)
relaunch.new_end_utc: 2026-10-19T16:01:00Z (end event; the freeze and scoring follow)
relaunch.day_window: day d = [START + (d-1) x 24 h, START + d x 24 h), 16:00 to 16:00 UTC

schedule.generated_by: testbed/e9/e9ops.py schedule --start 2026-10-12T16:00:00Z --days 7 --trials 5 --ec-arms PU PSR --e7-arms INS-L BD-S --keep-days 30 (the amendment-1 code, run with the pinned interpreter)

times_utc.nights: 03:40 sleep guard, 03:55 snapshot, 04:07 PURGE issuer (marker 04:10), 04:12 the hub's purge, 04:45 snapshot; first night 2026-10-13

choice: 16:00 UTC is outside the refused START window (03:40, 04:45].
The batch at 18:00 follows the 17:00 name-map session (about 6 min in the smoke runs) and precedes the 20:00 events; the harness runs events in order, so a collision would only delay one.
The special events keep amendment 2's dates and times; the nights are the same seven.
The hub restarted at 13:25 UTC in the teardown, so its next purge is 2026-10-13 04:12 (night 1), after the full-history seal, under its operator marker.

interpreter.how: the launcher (HOMEPROV-P13-exp/e9/launch_e9_amend3.sh, outside the frozen set) prepends <home>/miniconda3/bin to PATH, so run_e9.sh's command -v python3 resolves to it, and refuses to start unless that python3 is version 3.13.11 and opens a WAL-mode SQLite copy read-only

relaunch.unchanged: the 36 frozen files at their registered digests (testbed/e9/e9ops.py at amendment 1's), parameters, arms, benign events, outcomes, exclusions and the scoring; checked at registration (all match)
